title: The Wrap: Round 11 Clinic, Northern Lights & Double Header Fever

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: G'day legends and welcome to The Wrap, your weekly dose of touch footy gold for Point Takeaway down at Redlands Touch Association! Mick here, and oh boy, <short pause> Round 11 was an absolute pearler! Cleveland Showgrounds turned on a bit of pre-game drizzle, had all eleven of us huddled under the rusty tin roof, and then right on kickoff <sighs> the skies cleared, the turf gripped, and the boys dished out a proper 7 to 2 shellacking to the Redlands Centurions! <laugh> You beauty!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: A clinical performance, Mick. Particularly impressive considering our mate Nev decided looking at green skies in Norway for the Northern Lights was more important than freezing his backside off in Cleveland. <chuckle> So without Nev, the gaffer Graeme had eleven troops locked and loaded: Cam, Matt, BJ, Jayden, Reece, Mitch, Mack, Adrian, Joely, Dylan, and Peter. Though I must say, <short pause> minute one had a few blokes coughing up their tuckshop pies when Centurions crossed immediately to make it nil-one.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: <laughter> Stone the crows Gazza, talk about a wake-up call! <gasp> And then Peter produces the play of the century by getting penalised for colliding straight into his own teammate! <laugh> The ref didn't know what to blow, the sideline was in stitches, and Peter looked like he'd just tackled a ghost! <chuckle> But fair dinkum, once that cobweb cleared, Jayden sliced straight through the line and fed Joely for a cool-headed dot down to level it 1-all!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: Pure class from Joely. Then Cam stepped up into first receiver and delivered an absolute tracer bullet pass out wide to Mack, who crashed over right in the corner to make it 2-1. Centurions managed to scramble back to 2-all shortly after, despite Mack nearly dislocating a shoulder pulling off a heroic diving tag. <pant> But Peter quickly made amends for his friendly fire incident, dishing a sweet pill to Reece to regain the lead at 3-2.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: And right before the halftime hooter, Jayden and Dylan put on an absolute clinic through the middle! Give and go, draw and pass, slicing them to ribbons like a hot knife through butter to send us into the sheds up 4-2! <chuckle> The banter at the break was sensational, and whatever Graeme put in the water bottles worked wonders because Mitch came straight out of the sheds and scored an outrageous solo try to blow it out to 5-2!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: Mitch made five blokes look like parking cones on that run, Mick. <snicker> Sublime individual try. But then, the match official decided he wanted his own headline with the rare Cleveland double soft send-off. Mack gets sent for a walk to cool his heels on the sideline, and twenty seconds later Joely gets marched off right behind him. The sideline yelled out asking what for, and the ref deadpan replied, quote, it is a referee thing. <short pause> Tactical genius at work right there.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: <cackle> Bloody oath, a referee thing! I'm going to use that at work on Monday! But playing down numbers didn't bother the lads one bit. We get a tap penalty, the sideline literally screams out, no, don't do it! And Reece completely ignores the call, flicks on the turbo afterburners, burns their entire backline, and slams it down for 6-2! <laugh> You can't coach speed like that, mate!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: Reece doesn't take advice from the cheap seats, Mick, he just takes tries. <chuckle> Then Adrian produced an ankle-breaker in the middle of the paddock that sent two Centurions defenders sliding halfway to the Redlands clubhouse. <gasp> And to put the cherry on the cake, Cam, who simply never stops digging into the contest, chased down a loose ball, beat the cover defence, and sealed the emphatic 7-2 win right on the hooter.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: What a win! <sigh> And the gaffer Graeme was absolutely purring on the sideline after the match! He gave his official post-match appraisal to the group: <short pause> We played near to our best tonight. And it is good. Great to watch. When Graeme drops praise like that, you know the boys earned their post-game frothies!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: High praise indeed from the gaffer Graeme. Now, let's have a squiz at the other division results around Redlands. The Touchers took care of business against United, winning 8 to 2. Second-placed Hunt and Kill took down the Screws 6 to 2. And Bonsai kept themselves right in the hunt with an 8 to 3 victory over The Well Hungarians.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: Strewth, that sets up a wild ladder! Have a squiz at this: <short pause> The Touchers sit in first on 17 points, Hunt and Kill sit second on 17 points, and right up their clobber in third spot is Point Takeaway on 16 points with a plus 11 differential! And check this stat Gazza: <gasp> we've got the outright best attack in the entire competition with 47 tries scored! Bonsai are right on our tail in fourth on 16 points as well!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: Which brings us to next week, Wednesday the twenty-first of October on Field 6. It's the mother of all assignments. A double header against the top two teams on the ladder. <short pause> Game one taps off at quarter past eight Brisvegas time against number two Hunt and Kill. Then thirty minutes later, on the same field at quarter to nine, we back it up against the ladder leaders, The Touchers.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: Stone the crows! Back-to-back grudge matches against first and second! If the Point Takeaway machine clicks like it did against Centurions, we blow this minor premiership wide open! <laughter> Get your strapping tape ready, hydrate up, and we'll see all the faithful down at Cleveland Showgrounds on Wednesday night. Up the Point Takeaway!

title: The Wrap: 5-on-5 Field Day, 4-Try Feasts & The Showboat Special

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: G'day legends and welcome back to The Wrap, your weekly hit of touch footy gold for Point Takeaway at Redlands Touch Association! Mick here with Gazza, and oh boy... Round 10 was an absolute turkey shoot! Field 5 down at Cleveland Showgrounds, and fair dinkum, we turned up to find the Screws only had four blokes! <laugh> Four! So the gaffer Graeme and the boys agreed to a gentlemen's agreement, played five-on-five on a full-sized paddock, and dished out an almighty 13 to 4 shellacking! <laugh> You beauty!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: A proper open-field track meet, Mick. Playing five-on-five meant the defensive gaps weren't just big, they were like the Grand Canyon. We had eleven troops ready to roll, with only Adrian missing on a family holiday to Thailand, which meant our sub bench was practically overflowing. And it was a massive night for our flyer Reece, finally back on the paddock after six months on the sidelines with injury. ... Cam got the party started early, finding his brother Matt slicing straight through a yawning gap to make it 1-nil.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: Haha! Screws managed to snag an equalizer shortly after to make it 1-all, but then the fireworks kicked off! Jayden puts on the turbo jets, slices the line, but gets cruelly called back for a phantom touch before the dot down. <gasp> But twenty seconds later, Jayden dishes a sweet pill to Dylan in the corner to make it 2-1! And then Mitch, <chuckle> Mitch puts on a clinic, running sideways across the entire park, dodging five blokes, and crashing over for 3-1! You couldn't catch him with a lasso, mate!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: Mitch's vision in space was exceptional. Peter then got in on the act, sneaking right through the middle after Jayden earned six more to push it out to 4-1. Screws pulled one back in the corner for 4-2, before Joely probed the line, spotted Reece on his return, and fed him an absolute gift for 5-2. ... Then Mitch pulled off a gorgeous one-two give-and-go with Jayden through the ruck to make it 6-2.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: Stone the crows Gazza, and then the ref produces a comedy special right on halftime! <laugh> Matt pulls off a textbook tag on their runner, the bloke just ignores it, keeps running, grounds the ball, and the ref gives the try for 6-3! Haha! The sideline was yelling out, but into the sheds we went with a healthy three-try buffer! And mate, whatever Graeme said at halftime, Dylan took it personally!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: Dylan came out of the sheds like a startled gazelle, Mick. Screws had first ball in the second half, turned it over, and Dylan scooped it up from our own tryline and ran seventy meters untouched down the touchline to make it 7-3. <chuckle> Screws managed to strike back to 7-4, and to their credit they were playing smart footy, but five-on-five touch footy is brutal on the lungs and they were blowing like draft horses.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: They were completely out of puff, Gazza! And that's when Peter turned on the razzle-dazzle! <gasp> He gets the ball, pulls off an ankle-breaking double step that sent two defenders into next week, and waltzed over for 8-4! Then Mack started rucking like a man possessed, laying a platform for Jayden to dish to Joely to make it 9-4! But Gazza — talk to me about Dylan's hat-trick try!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: <chuckle> The showboat of the season, Mick. Graeme noted it officially in the team dispatches. Dylan gets the ball on the outside, waves and shows the ball to the Screws defender as he cruises past, and dots it down for 10-4. Graeme literally wrote in his notes, quote, I say, over and out. <laugh> Ruthless disrespect from Dylan, you've got to love it.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: <laugh> 'I say, over and out!' That is legendary from the gaffer Graeme! And we weren't done yet! Cam, Peter, and Jayden marched us fifty meters upfield, dished to Mitch on the burst, and he streaks away for his hat-trick to blow it out to 11-4! Then Peter and Reece trade sweet passes before Matt feeds Mitch again for his fourth try of the night to make it 12-4! Four tries for Mitch, you beauty!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: Four tries for Mitch, but the play of the night came in defence right after. Screws broke through our line against the run of play, their winger thought he was home, and Mack turned on the jetpack, chased him down from twenty meters back, and pulled off a miraculous diving tag right on our tryline. ... Pure hustle from Mack.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: Diving tag of the year, mate! And then to put the icing on the cake, Matt steps, jumps, draws two defenders, and feeds Dylan for his fourth try of the evening to seal the 13 to 4 rout right on the final hooter! <laugh> Four tries for Dylan, four tries for Mitch, ten different try assists, and a glorious night at the Showgrounds!

transcript.speaker: Gazza
transcript.text: A dominant, highly entertaining victory. And the gaffer Graeme summed up the evening with trademark serenity: ... The Full time siren sounded to end an enjoyable night out. FT 13-4. When you put thirteen past an opponent and leave the park with a plus nine differential, that is certainly an enjoyable night out.

transcript.speaker: Mick
transcript.text: <sigh> Too right, Gazza! That thirteen-try explosion set the stage for our Round 11 masterclass against the Centurions, and sets us right up for the top-of-the-table double header! What a team, what a club! Up the Point Takeaway!
